label: position subscriber automation
summary: Plan position lifecycle automation through a subscriber or keeper while preserving modification liveness, distrust of reported fees, and user exit.
requiredFacts: Exact PositionManager and subscriber deployments, ownership, upgrade, allowlisting, callback gas and notification behavior
Which subscribe, modify, transfer, burn and unsubscribe calls can revert and the required PoolManager lock state
User-controlled unsubscribe and position modification path even when the subscriber is malicious or unavailable
Why callback feesAccrued is untrusted and which independently reconciled state governs rewards, eligibility or accounting
Keeper trigger, authentication, funding, duplicate suppression, stale state, fallback, monitoring and retirement
requiredFiles: Pinned PositionManager, subscriber and keeper source closure
Gas, liveness, unsubscribe and user-exit specification
Independent position and fee reconciliation source
Executable callback, donation and keeper failure tests
requiredTests: Subscriber revert and gas exhaustion on subscribe, modify, burn and unsubscribe
Donation-inflated feesAccrued and no payout, score or eligibility trust in that callback value
PoolManager lock-state ordering, transfer, approval, subscriber upgrade, code removal and malicious callback
Keeper outage, duplicate job, stale block, reorg, unauthorized trigger, depleted funding and recovery
User unsubscribe, liquidity removal, fee collection, burn, migration and exit under every failure state
risks: A subscriber is an execution dependency that can make position operations revert
Callback feesAccrued can be deliberately inflated through donation and cannot authenticate revenue
Automation can centralize liveness or authority in a keeper even when the position NFT appears user-owned
